priority.formExplanation: A current report — the form companies use to disclose material events between quarters (deals, leadership changes, results, financings).
priority.summary: Fermi Inc. discloses the immediate resignation of director Miles Everson, effective July 10, 2026, due to a disagreement over access to company books and records and the delegation of responsibility to the Finance Committee for overseeing financing transactions. Everson's resignation was submitted in a letter, which is attached to the filing as an exhibit, and he did not serve on any committee of the Board at the time of his resignation. The company believes Everson was granted full access to its books and records, except for materials related to pending litigation involving Toby Neugebauer, whom Everson represented on the Board.

priority.summary: Fermi Inc. commenced an offering for the sale of $350 million aggregate principal amount of convertible senior notes due 2031 to qualified institutional buyers, with an option to purchase up to an additional $52.5 million aggregate principal amount of notes. Fermi Inc. also disclosed that it has deferred its election to be taxed as a real estate investment trust for US federal income tax purposes, and now expects to qualify and elect to be taxed as a REIT commencing with its taxable year ending December 31, 2026.

Neugebauer, co-founder and largest shareholder of Fermi Inc., disclosed that the company has dropped its lawsuit against him, which was filed to validate a 70% supermajority bylaw amendment, after a Texas Business Court ordered the company to produce documents and testimony explaining the rationale for the bylaw. The move is seen as a significant development in the ongoing governance dispute at Fermi, with Neugebauer arguing that the board's actions were an attempt to entrench itself and avoid scrutiny.

general.summary: Health authorities in Kenya confirmed an Ebola infection in a traveler who recently arrived from the Democratic Republic of Congo.
